AgentCommand.description:
One of the agent's slash commands or skills (v0.11 item 66), for the composer's list.

``name`` has no ``/`` (``standup``, ``acme:review``); ``description`` is
one line (its first sentence); ``source`` is where the engine says it
comes from (``user``, ``project``, a plug-in's name), when it says.
AgentCommand.title: AgentCommand

AgentFinished.description: A subagent ended (v0.10); ``summary`` is the first line of what it reported.
AgentFinished.title: AgentFinished

AgentProgress.description: What a subagent is doing now (v0.10): its current ``step``, its tool calls so far, seconds since it started.
AgentProgress.title: AgentProgress

AgentStarted.description:
A subagent started (v0.10).

``id`` names the agent in the frames that follow; ``tool_use_id`` is the
call that started it (a workflow's agents share the workflow's call).
``kind`` is the agent type the engine names (e.g. ``general-purpose``),
or ``workflow`` for one of a workflow's agents, which also carries
``workflow_id`` and ``phase`` (an index into ``workflow.started``'s
``phases``). ``background`` is set when the agent runs on after its
turn finishes.
AgentStarted.title: AgentStarted

AppCallResult.description: v0.18: the answer to ``app.call_tool`` (its ``id``). ``ok`` false carries ``error``; the result is never the model's.
AppCallResult.title: AppCallResult

AppCallTool.description: v0.18: the page asks to run ``tool`` on its own server (a bare name means that server's).
AppCallTool.title: AppCallTool

AppCancelled.description: v0.18: the call ended with no result (stopped, or an error before one).
AppCancelled.title: AppCancelled

AppContext.description: v0.18: the page's ``ui/update-model-context``: kept (latest only) and put before the person's next message.
AppContext.title: AppContext

AppMessage.description: v0.18: the page's ``ui/message``: sent as the person's message, labelled ``via`` the app.
AppMessage.title: AppMessage

AppOpen.description:
v0.18: show the app card for the agent's call ``tool_use_id``.

``server`` is the configured name, ``server_title`` what to call it
(``serverInfo.title``, else the name); ``tool`` is the bare tool name.
``html`` is the page (absent in a replay: the card comes back frozen).
``csp``, ``permissions`` and ``prefers_border`` are the resource's
``_meta.ui`` members, as the server gave them.
AppOpen.title: AppOpen

AppReload.description: v0.18: read the page again (starting the chat's engine if needed); answered ``app.open`` then ``app.result``.
AppReload.title: AppReload

AppResult.description: v0.18: the call's result for the page (``structured_content`` absent when it was over the cap).
AppResult.title: AppResult

CardAnswered.description:
The card ``id`` was answered (``card.answer`` accepted); it is closed.

Stamped and kept in the ring, so a replay that carries the ``card.ask``
also carries its closing and the app does not pin the card again.
CardAnswered.title: CardAnswered

ChatCommands.description:
The agent's commands and skills in ``folder``, for slash completion (v0.11 item 66).

Sent with ``chat`` after that chat's engine starts; sent without it on
connect, from the list the gateway kept for the folder, so the welcome
has one before any engine runs. A reading, not history: no ``seq``.
ChatCommands.title: ChatCommands

ChatCompacted.description: The engine summarized earlier conversation to make room.
ChatCompacted.title: ChatCompacted

ChatNotice.description: A quiet line in the conversation from the gateway, e.g. an unknown command.
ChatNotice.title: ChatNotice

ChatQueue.description:
The messages a chat holds for the agent, oldest first, after every change (v0.11).

Sent when one is queued, unqueued, or goes to the agent, and after
``chat.live`` on every ``chat.open`` (an empty list too), so a
reconnecting app sees what is still waiting. Not in the ring: the list
as it stands replaces whatever the app had.

``returned`` (v0.11, Larry 10-30): messages taken out of the queue by
``turn.stop``, oldest first, for the app to put back in the composer
(text and attachments) to send again or delete. Absent otherwise.
ChatQueue.title: ChatQueue

ChatQueued.description:
The answer to a ``message.send`` that arrived during a turn or the log step (v0.11).

The message is held, not refused: ``id`` is the request's (the queued
message's id from now on). Only to an app that declared ``queue.v1``;
an older app still gets ``error code=chat.busy``.
ChatQueued.title: ChatQueued

ChatUnqueue.description:
Take a queued message (``id``, as ``chat.queued`` named it) off the queue before it goes (v0.11).

Answered with the ``chat.queue`` that follows, or ``error
code=chat.not_queued`` when it has already gone to the agent (or was
never queued). An edit is this, then a new ``message.send``.
ChatUnqueue.title: ChatUnqueue

ClientMessage.description: Any app -> gateway message, discriminated on type.

ConfigStale.description: The config file changed after the gateway started; restart the gateway to apply it.
ConfigStale.title: ConfigStale

ContextUsage.description: How full the session's context window is, after each turn.
ContextUsage.title: ContextUsage

FilesRoots.description: v0.19: the roots this connection has: the deployment's, then the person's added folders in order.
FilesRoots.title: FilesRoots

FilesRootsSet.description: v0.19 (``files.extra.v1``): the folders this connection adds to the Files pane; replaces the last list.
FilesRootsSet.title: FilesRootsSet

FilesSearch.description: Search names and text under a root; answered with ``files.results``.
FilesSearch.title: FilesSearch

GatewayStop.description:
Stop the gateway: interrupt every running turn, run ``on_stop``, exit.

Distinct from quitting the app, which only detaches.
GatewayStop.title: GatewayStop

Hit.description: One search result: ``path`` is relative to the searched root.
Hit.title: Hit

McpAdd.description:
v0.18: add a server (``claude mcp add``): by a web address (``url``) or a program on this Mac (``command``).

``where`` is ``user`` (All your projects) or ``local`` (this agent only).
McpAdd.title: McpAdd

McpList.description: v0.18: the servers as Settings shows them.
McpList.title: McpList

McpReconnect.description: v0.18: reconnect a server in every live engine on Settings' folder.
McpReconnect.title: McpReconnect

McpRemove.description: v0.18: remove a user or local server (``claude mcp remove``); the app asks first.
McpRemove.title: McpRemove

McpServerRow.description: One server as Settings shows it. ``detail`` is the status line; group titles and brand words are the app's.
McpServerRow.title: McpServerRow

McpServers.title: McpServers

McpSignIn.description: v0.18: sign in to a server (``claude mcp login``): answered at once, then a fresh ``mcp.servers`` (no id) when done.
McpSignIn.title: McpSignIn

McpSignOut.description: v0.18: sign out of a server (``claude mcp logout``).
McpSignOut.title: McpSignOut

McpToggle.description: v0.18: turn a server off (``enabled`` false) or on again, for Settings' folder; from the next engine start.
McpToggle.title: McpToggle

McpToolPolicy.description: v0.18: whether one tool runs without asking (``allow``) or asks first (``ask``); ``null`` is back to the default.
McpToolPolicy.title: McpToolPolicy

McpToolRow.description: One tool of a server: ``policy`` is the effective one (the person's choice, else the default).
McpToolRow.title: McpToolRow

ModelChoice.description:
v0.15: one entry of the engine's model list, the CLI's ``/model`` list.

``value`` is what ``model.set`` sends back (``opus``, ``sonnet``,
``claude-fable-5-1[1m]``, ``default``); ``display_name`` and
``description`` are the engine's own words. ``resolved_model`` (11-02)
is the model id the entry runs (the engine's ``resolvedModel``), so the
app can name what Default resolves to; absent when the engine did not
say, and an older app ignores it.
ModelChoice.title: ModelChoice

ModelSet.description:
v0.15: switch the model for this session and the ones after it (``models.v1``).

``value`` is a ``ModelChoice.value`` from ``models``; ``"default"`` or
``null`` is the deployment's default. Answered by ``models`` carrying the
request's ``id`` and the new ``current``, or by ``error``: ``chat.busy``
while a reply runs, ``model.unknown`` for a value the list lacks.
ModelSet.title: ModelSet

Models.description:
v0.15: the models the session can switch to and the one it runs on (``models.v1``).

Sent after ``hello`` for each live session (from the list the gateway
kept), after each engine start, and after a switch (with the
``model.set`` request's ``id``). ``current`` is the model this session
runs on: its running engine's, else the stored choice it will start on;
absent (``null``) is the deployment's default. A reading, not history:
no ``seq``.
Models.title: Models

PluginMarketplace.description:
One marketplace. ``source_label`` is its repo or path (``None`` for the official one); ``checked`` is
"today", "yesterday" or a date like "Oct 24" (the newest change in its checkout), or "" when unknown.
PluginMarketplace.title: PluginMarketplace

PluginOption.description: One option of a plugin. A sensitive option's value is never sent: ``value`` is null and ``set`` says whether it has one.
PluginOption.title: PluginOption

PluginRow.description:
One installed plugin. ``description`` and ``marketplace`` come from its marketplace entry, joined by id.

``update_to`` is the marketplace's version when it differs from the installed one.
PluginRow.title: PluginRow

PluginsConfigure.description: v0.18: save option values (only the changed ones), piped to ``claude plugin configure <id> --values-stdin``.
PluginsConfigure.title: PluginsConfigure

PluginsDetails.description: v0.18: a plugin's ``claude plugin details`` text.
PluginsDetails.title: PluginsDetails

PluginsDetailsRequest.description: v0.18: a plugin's inventory as text (``claude plugin details <id>``).
PluginsDetailsRequest.title: PluginsDetailsRequest

PluginsInstall.description: v0.18: install a plugin (``claude plugin install <id> --json``); one that installs by running a command is refused.
PluginsInstall.title: PluginsInstall

PluginsList.description: v0.18: the installed plugins and the marketplaces; ``available`` true adds what the marketplaces offer.
PluginsList.title: PluginsList

PluginsMarketplaceAdd.description: v0.18: add a marketplace (``claude plugin marketplace add <source>``): owner/repo, a git address or a path.
PluginsMarketplaceAdd.title: PluginsMarketplaceAdd

PluginsMarketplaceUpdate.description: v0.18: check a marketplace for updates (``claude plugin marketplace update <name>``).
PluginsMarketplaceUpdate.title: PluginsMarketplaceUpdate

PluginsOptions.description: v0.18: a plugin's options (empty: nothing to configure).
PluginsOptions.title: PluginsOptions

PluginsOptionsRequest.description: v0.18: a plugin's options (``claude plugin configure <id> --json``).
PluginsOptionsRequest.title: PluginsOptionsRequest

PluginsSetEnabled.description: v0.18: turn a plugin on or off (``claude plugin enable|disable <id> --scope <its scope>``).
PluginsSetEnabled.title: PluginsSetEnabled

PluginsState.description:
v0.18: the answer to ``plugins.list`` and to every plugin change (with the request's ``id``).

``available`` is present only when the request was a ``plugins.list`` with
``available: true``. A reading, not history: no ``seq``.
PluginsState.title: PluginsState

PluginsUninstall.description: v0.18: uninstall a plugin (``claude plugin uninstall <id> --scope <its scope>``); the app asks first.
PluginsUninstall.title: PluginsUninstall

PluginsUpdate.description: v0.18: update a plugin to its marketplace's version (``claude plugin update <id>``).
PluginsUpdate.title: PluginsUpdate

QueuedMessage.description:
A message the person sent during a turn, held by the gateway until it goes (v0.11).

``id`` is the ``message.send`` request's ``id`` (one the gateway made
up when the request had none); ``text`` and ``attachments`` are as sent.
QueuedMessage.title: QueuedMessage

ServerMessage.description: Any gateway -> app message, discriminated on type.

Service.description:
One of the deployment's services (v0.4), as its check last found it.

``since`` is when the current state began (ISO 8601 UTC); ``detail`` one
line for the menu; ``can_restart`` whether the deployment gave it a
``restart`` command.
Service.title: Service

ServiceRestart.description:
Run a service's ``restart`` command, then check it again (v0.4).

Answered by the ``services.status`` that follows. v0.8: refused with
``services.busy`` while a ``services.restart_all`` runs.
ServiceRestart.title: ServiceRestart

ServicesRestartAll.description:
Restart all the deployment's services with its one restart command (v0.8).

Only when ``hello.capabilities`` has ``services.restart_all``. No
``services.status`` goes out while it runs; the one read after the
restart is the answer. A restart that fails also answers, after that
status, with ``error code=services.restart_failed`` carrying the
request's ``id``.
ServicesRestartAll.title: ServicesRestartAll

ServicesStatus.description: Every deployment service and its state, down ones first (v0.4).
ServicesStatus.title: ServicesStatus

SessionLog.description:
Run the deployment's log step in the live session ``chat`` without ending it (v0.4).

Answered with ``session.logged`` then ``chat.list``.
SessionLog.title: SessionLog

SessionLogged.description: The log step ``session.log`` asked for has run; ``chat`` is the session's summary now (v0.4).
SessionLogged.title: SessionLogged

SessionMode.description: Change the session's permission mode; answered with ``chat.state`` carrying ``mode``.
SessionMode.title: SessionMode

SessionRenew.description:
End the session ``chat`` and start the next one in the same folder.

With ``log`` the gateway first runs the deployment's log step in the
ending session and waits for it. Answered with ``session.renewed``.
SessionRenew.title: SessionRenew

SessionRenewed.description: The session ``ended`` was closed and ``next`` is the live one now.
SessionRenewed.title: SessionRenewed

SessionsClear.description:
Forget the ended sessions, keeping the live one (v0.11, single presentation only).

Only when ``hello.capabilities`` has ``sessions.clear``. Only Portico's
list is cleared: the engine's transcripts on disk stay, and the numbers
are never handed out again. Answered with ``chat.list``; refused with
``sessions.not_single`` in multiple presentation.
SessionsClear.title: SessionsClear

SpaceInfo.description: One space in ``spaces.list``: ``updated`` is the file's modification time (UTC ISO 8601).
SpaceInfo.title: SpaceInfo

SpaceRefresh.description: v0.12: run the deployment's refresh for a space; ``id`` is the space's id. Answered by ``spaces.list`` or ``error``.
SpaceRefresh.title: SpaceRefresh

SpaceRemove.description: v0.12: move a space's file to the Trash and run the deployment's remove; ``id`` is the space's id.
SpaceRemove.title: SpaceRemove

SpaceRename.description: v0.12: set a space's title (written into its front matter); ``id`` is the space's id.
SpaceRename.title: SpaceRename

SpacesList.description: v0.12: the spaces as they are, after ``services.status`` on hello and whenever the folder changes.
SpacesList.title: SpacesList

ThreadClose.description:
v0.16: close the thread ``chat``: its log step, then it ends into History.

``log`` false skips the log step (the thread ends ``logged: false``): the
app's "Close without logging" after a close whose log step cannot start.
ThreadClose.title: ThreadClose

ThreadDismiss.description: v0.16: "Not now" on a proposal on Main (``chat``); its record reads "Not started".
ThreadDismiss.title: ThreadDismiss

ThreadInfo.description:
What makes a chat a thread (v0.16): opened from Main (``parent``) for ``brief``.

``label`` is "Thread 1" or "Thread 2"; ``slot`` is its number, the key
that switches to it (a closed thread's slot is used again); ``files``
are the paths it started with; ``opened_at`` when it was started.
ThreadInfo.title: ThreadInfo

ThreadProposal.description:
v0.16: a thread Main's agent proposed (``open_thread``), and where it stands.

``chat`` is Main's; ``proposal`` the proposal's id; ``tool_use_id`` the
``open_thread`` tool row the card is drawn in place of. ``thread`` is the
chat it started, once ``state`` is ``started``. A state frame like
``chat.queue``: not in the ring, sent on every change and after
``chat.live`` on every ``chat.open``. Only to an app with ``threads.v1``.
ThreadProposal.title: ThreadProposal

ThreadStart.description:
v0.16: start the thread a proposal on Main (``chat``) describes (``threads.v1``).

``close`` names an open thread to close first when two are open (the
limit card's Close and start). Starting does not change which chat is Main.
ThreadStart.title: ThreadStart

UpdateAvailable.description: The deployment's update check found a newer version.
UpdateAvailable.title: UpdateAvailable

UserText.description:
What the person sent to start a turn (v0.19: as typed, with ``attachments`` apart).

Live, right after ``turn.started`` (stamped, in the ring), and in a
transcript replay (``chat.history``, unstamped): one rendering path
for the person's words whichever way the conversation arrives.
UserText.title: UserText

ViewerAct.description:
v0.12: the agent acts in the viewer; the app answers with ``viewer.result`` carrying the same ``id``.

v0.17: ``show`` (``{artifact, location}``), only to an app that declared
``viewer.show.v1``, is answered once the shown page has loaded.
ViewerAct.title: ViewerAct

ViewerDefaults.description: v0.12: the deployment's viewer settings (config ``[viewer]``), sent in ``hello``.
ViewerDefaults.title: ViewerDefaults

ViewerResult.description: v0.12: the app's answer to a ``viewer.act``.
ViewerResult.title: ViewerResult

ViewerSettings.description: v0.12: the person's two viewer switches; sent after ``hello`` and when either changes. Not chat-scoped.
ViewerSettings.title: ViewerSettings

WorkflowPhase.description: One workflow phase changed state (v0.10); ``index`` is into ``workflow.started``'s ``phases``.
WorkflowPhase.title: WorkflowPhase

WorkflowStarted.description: A workflow started (v0.10). Sent again with the same ``id`` when its phases become known or change.
WorkflowStarted.title: WorkflowStarted

description: Messages between the Portico app (client) and a gateway (server).
title: Portico protocol
